title: SMT solver backend (Z3)
description: Z3 is the workhorse SMT solver: feed it formulas over integers, reals, bitvectors, arrays, and it answers SAT/UNSAT with models or proofs. Prover integrations use Z3 as the automated backend for discharging verification conditions — the 'just solve it' engine behind Dafny, F*, and countless CI checks.
method: Encode the verification condition in SMT-LIB; Z3 decides satisfiability; SAT gives a counterexample model, UNSAT proves the property.
usage: Keep formulas in decidable fragments where possible; use unsat cores to debug failing proofs.

demo.code:
print('SMT-LIB: (assert (> x 5)) (assert (< x 3))')
print('Z3: UNSAT — no integer is both >5 and <3 (property proved)')

title: Tactic-based proof automation
description: Tactics are proof-search programs inside assistants: 'simp', 'omega', 'ring' discharge whole classes of goals automatically. Good tactic libraries mean humans prove the interesting steps and automation handles the routine — the division of labor that makes mechanized proof affordable.
method: Apply domain tactics to goals; they perform search/simplification; remaining goals get human attention; custom tactics encode domain knowledge.
usage: Build a tactic library per domain; prefer robust tactics over brittle exact-step scripts.

demo.code:
print('goal: (a + b) * 2 = 2 * a + 2 * b')
print('tactic: ring -> CLOSED (no human steps needed)')

title: Verified compilation (CompCert)
description: CompCert is a C compiler proved correct in Coq: the generated assembly is proved to preserve the semantics of the source for every input. Integrating verified compilation means the toolchain itself can't introduce bugs — the strongest link in the verification chain.
method: Compiler passes proved as semantics-preserving simulations in Coq; the extracted compiler carries the proof; use for safety-critical builds.
usage: Use verified compilation for the critical components; the proof covers the compiler, not your source logic.

demo.code:
print('CompCert: 12 passes, each proved semantics-preserving')
print('build: critical controller compiled with CompCert -> no miscompilation possible')

title: Hammer-style ATP integration
description: Hammers (CoqHammer, Sledgehammer for Isabelle) translate the current goal to first-order logic, farm it out to automated theorem provers (E, Vampire, Z3), and reconstruct the found proof inside the assistant. Interactive proving gets an 'ask the machines' button that closes routine goals automatically.
method: Translate goal + relevant lemmas to FOL; run ATPs in parallel with time limits; reconstruct the proof from the ATP's output in the assistant's kernel.
usage: Curate the lemma set the hammer sees (too many slows it, too few starves it); use hammers for routine goals.

demo.code:
print('goal: list lemma; hammer translates to FOL, runs E + Vampire')
print('Vampire finds proof in 2.1s -> reconstructed in Coq kernel: CLOSED')

title: Model-based prover debugging
description: When the prover says 'can't prove it', its model (counterexample) shows a concrete scenario violating the property — often revealing the spec is wrong, not the code. Reading prover models turns failed proofs into debugging sessions instead of dead ends.
method: On failure, extract the solver's model; map it back to program variables; inspect: is the code wrong, or is the spec too strong?
usage: Always read the counterexample before weakening the spec; most failed proofs teach something.

demo.code:
print('failed: ensures result > 0')
print('model: x = 0 -> result = 0')
print('diagnosis: spec too strong (x=0 valid input) -> fix spec, re-prove: OK')

title: Proof-carrying CI artifacts
description: Build artifacts ship with their proofs: the binary plus a machine-checkable certificate that it satisfies its spec. Downstream consumers verify the certificate in milliseconds without re-running the prover — trust the proof, not the build machine.
method: Prover emits (artifact, proof); the proof checker is small and fast; deployment gates on proof validity.
usage: Keep the checker tiny and audited; gate deployments on proof validity for critical components.

demo.code:
print('artifact: controller.bin + proof.cert')
print('deploy gate: checker verifies cert in 40ms -> VALID, deploy proceeds')

title: Proof replay in CI
description: Proofs rot like tests when code changes — proof replay re-runs the full mechanized proof suite on every commit, catching the moment a code change breaks a proof. The proof suite is a CI job like any other: green means the guarantees still hold.
method: Check in proof scripts with code; CI runs the proof checker; failures block merge; proof maintenance is part of the change.
usage: Keep proofs fast enough for CI (cache aggressively); assign proof repair with the code change.

demo.code:
print('CI: lean --make ... 142 theorems checked')
print('result: all proved in 38s -> MERGE')

title: Boogie intermediate verification language
description: Boogie is the shared intermediate layer: frontends (Dafny, VCC) compile programs and specs to Boogie, which generates verification conditions for Z3. One solid VC generator serves many languages — the LLVM of program verification.
method: Frontend emits Boogie (procedures + specs); Boogie computes weakest preconditions; Z3 proves them; errors map back to source.
usage: Build new verifiers on Boogie rather than from scratch; map errors back to source locations carefully.

demo.code:
print('Dafny -> Boogie -> VC -> Z3')
print('Boogie: 14 verification conditions, 14 proved')
